In 1812, a man from Switzerland was travelling in Jordan. He heard about

Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago. It had gardens with fountains and ponds

Archaeologists aren’t sure why the Nabataeans carved the stone here. Some
think it was for a king, while others believe it was a temple. Amazingly, most of
the city is still underground!
In ancient Rome, now in Italy, there was a city called Herculaneum. About
2,000 years ago, a volcano called Vesuvius erupted and covered the city.
In 1738, archaeologists started to dig, and today people can visit the city. There
are streets, houses, shops, cafés and small factories. Visitors can see the houses
with paintings on the walls. There are also pools, bath houses and a theatre.
